newsitem.title: USA: Board denies parole for Robert Kennedy's assassin.
newsitem.headline: Board denies parole for Robert Kennedy's assassin.

text.p: Sirhan Sirhan, convicted of assassinating presidential candidate Robert Kennedy in 1968, was denied parole for the 10th time on Wednesday after protesting that he was innocent and had been framed.

A parole board unanimously turned down Sirhan's parole bid after an 80-minute hearing at Corcoran State Prison, 150 miles (240 kms) north of Los Angeles, said Liz Tanaka, a spokeswoman for the California Board of Prison Terms.

Sirhan, 53, was denied parole for the next three years. Wearing a light-blue shirt and with his black hair closely cropped, Sirhan gave a long speech to the parole board, saying he had uncovered evidence showing he was wrongly convicted of killing Kennedy.
Sirhan shot Kennedy on June 5, 1968, just after Kennedy had won the California Democratic presidential primary.
"The evidence that is there now and has been researched by my researcher and by my family shows that I was unjustly and wrongfully convicted for this crime," Sirhan told the board.

"There is demonstrable physical evidence that shows that gross injustice, deliberate injustice and ... just an out-and-out frameup of this case took place by the district attorney to convict me," he protested.
